validated_results.title: Alcohol consumption and PSA-detected prostate cancer risk--a case-control nested in the ProtecT study.
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study reporting associations of weekly alcohol consumption with PSA-detected prostate cancer risk by grade.

extraction.comparison_type: per 10 units/week increase in alcohol consumption, low Gleason-grade prostate cancer
extraction.timing: nested in the PSA-testing phase of the ProtecT randomized controlled trial
extraction.population: Men with PSA-detected prostate cancer and controls matched on age and general practice in the ProtecT PSA-testing phase

effect_size.excerpt: Linear and multinomial logistic regression models were used to estimate ratios of geometric means (RGMs) of PSA and relative risk ratios (RRRs) of prostate cancer by stage and grade, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), associated with weekly alcohol intake and drinking patterns. We found evidence of lower PSA (RGM 0.98, 95% CI: 0.98-0.99) and decreased risk of low Gleason-grade (RRR 0.96; 95%CI 0.93-0.99) but increased risk of high-grade prostate cancer (RRR 1.04; 95%CI 0.99-1.08; p(difference) =0.004) per 10 units/week increase in alcohol consumption, not explained by current BMI, blood pressure, comorbidities, or reverse causation.

confidence_interval.excerpt: We found evidence of lower PSA (RGM 0.98, 95% CI: 0.98-0.99) and decreased risk of low Gleason-grade (RRR 0.96; 95%CI 0.93-0.99) but increased risk of high-grade prostate cancer (RRR 1.04; 95%CI 0.99-1.08; p(difference) =0.004) per 10 units/week increase in alcohol consumption, not explained by current BMI, blood pressure, comorbidities, or reverse causation.
